difficultyRationale: The three annotations have distinct, documented, well-known scopes with no ambiguity once the names are known.
prompt: Which statement correctly characterizes Spring Boot's test-slice annotations @WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest, and @SpringBootTest?
explanation: Each slice loads only the beans relevant to the layer it targets, which keeps the test fast and focused. @WebMvcTest auto-configures MVC infrastructure and a MockMvc client, leaving services and repositories to be supplied as test doubles. @DataJpaTest auto-configures JPA-related infrastructure for repository tests, by default against an embedded test database. @SpringBootTest loads the full application context, for tests that need the whole wiring assembled.

options.text: @SpringBootTest is a lighter-weight slice than @WebMvcTest because it loads fewer beans, making it the default choice for fast controller tests.
options.explanation: This reverses the relationship: @SpringBootTest loads the full application context and is therefore the heavier of the two, while @WebMvcTest is the narrow slice meant for fast controller-focused tests.

options.text: @WebMvcTest loads only the web layer and auto-configures a MockMvc client, with collaborators supplied as mocks; @DataJpaTest loads only JPA infrastructure for repository tests against a test database; @SpringBootTest loads the full application context for broader tests.
options.explanation: This matches each annotation's documented scope: a narrow web slice, a narrow persistence slice, and the full context respectively, each sized to what the test actually needs.

options.text: @DataJpaTest starts a full embedded web server and the security filter chain so repository tests can exercise HTTP semantics, letting a single @DataJpaTest class double as an integration test for both the web tier and the security configuration without any additional setup at all.
options.explanation: @DataJpaTest is scoped to JPA infrastructure only; it does not start a web server or configure the security filter chain, since repository tests have nothing to do with HTTP handling.

options.text: @WebMvcTest and @DataJpaTest load the exact same set of beans, differing only in annotation name for readability.
options.explanation: The two annotations configure entirely different parts of the application context — MVC components for one, JPA and persistence components for the other — so their bean sets do not overlap in the way this option claims.
